title: Implement Alpaca activity and trade update stream normalization
description:
Implement broker activity ingestion and trade_updates stream normalization.

mike_trade/brokers/alpaca/activities.py:
(1) Query GET /v2/account/activities, by type and with date/after/until filters, through the e.1 client. Paginate using page_token and page_size with a hard maximum page count so reads are bounded.
(2) Normalize FILL activities: id, order_id, symbol, side, qty, cum_qty, leaves_qty, price, transaction_time in UTC, and type (fill or partial_fill). Normalize non-trade activities where present, such as fees (FEE, CFEE, PTC, and TAF-related where reported), dividends, and corporate actions (SPLIT, SPIN, MA, NC, and similar). All amounts are Decimal.
(3) Each normalized activity has a stable idempotency key, the broker activity id plus environment/account fingerprint, so repeated ingestion of the same activity is detectable and can be deduplicated downstream. Provide a pure dedupe helper.
(4) Unknown activity types are preserved as a raw, typed UnknownActivity rather than dropped or crashing.

mike_trade/brokers/alpaca/updates.py:
(1) Normalize trade_updates stream messages into a typed TradeUpdate covering at least: new/accepted, pending_new, partial_fill, fill, rejected, canceled, expired, replaced, pending_cancel, pending_replace, done_for_day, and stopped/suspended/calculated where documented. Include event, the full normalized order (Decimal filled_qty, filled_avg_price, hwm, stop_price, and so on), execution_id, price, qty, position_qty, and UTC timestamp. Partial fills must carry incremental and cumulative quantities correctly. Unknown events are preserved as typed unknowns.
(2) Implement a stream session/state machine over an injectable websocket transport protocol, with no real network access in tests. It authenticates with environment-matched credentials, subscribes to trade_updates (listen), and handles auth failure as a typed error.
(3) Reconnection uses bounded exponential backoff with jitter (injectable sleep) and a maximum attempt policy. Each reconnect emits an explicit Reconnected/Gap event so downstream reconciliation can query REST (open orders, orders by client_order_id, and activities since the last seen timestamp) to fill gaps. The session never assumes that no events were missed.
(4) Updates are tagged with environment/account fingerprint. A message arriving on a session whose environment does not match is rejected.
(5) This module only normalizes and emits. It never submits, cancels, or modifies orders.

Create tests/contracts/test_alpaca_trade_updates.py using JSON fixtures and fake transports, with no network access and no credentials. Positive and negative tests must cover: normalization of each listed event type; partial-fill then fill sequence quantities; Decimal fields; unknown event preservation; auth failure; that disconnect produces a Reconnected/Gap event followed by resubscription; that backoff is bounded by the injected sleep; activity pagination with a page cap; fill/fee/corporate activity normalization; idempotency-key stability and dedupe; and environment mismatch rejection.

Before editing, inspect: mike_trade/brokers/alpaca/http.py and auth.py (from e.1), account.py and assets.py (from e.2), any fill/activity/event domain types and the broker port from earlier phases, and existing async/clock abstractions. If orders.py from e.3 is present, reuse its order-normalization helper only when it exists. Otherwise implement a local normalizer and do not edit orders.py.
acceptance_criteria: activities.py paginates account activities with page_token and enforces a hard maximum page count, verified by a fixture test
FILL, fee, dividend, and corporate-action activities normalize to typed objects with Decimal amounts/quantities and UTC timestamps; unknown types become a typed UnknownActivity
Each normalized activity has a stable idempotency key including environment/account fingerprint; the dedupe helper removes duplicates on repeated ingestion

updates.py normalizes accepted/new, partial_fill, fill, rejected, canceled, expired, replaced, pending_cancel, and pending_replace trade_updates into a typed TradeUpdate with Decimal quantities and prices
A partial_fill followed by fill fixture yields correct incremental qty, cumulative filled_qty, and position_qty
Stream session authenticates, subscribes to trade_updates, and raises a typed error on auth failure
A simulated disconnect emits an explicit reconnect/gap event, resubscribes, and uses bounded backoff via the injected sleep (no real delay)
Messages whose environment does not match the session are rejected
Neither module calls any order submit/cancel/replace endpoint
tests/contracts/test_alpaca_trade_updates.py passes without network access or credentials
forbidden_changes: edit orders.py, http.py, auth.py, account.py, or assets.py
change PLAN_SKELETON.json or any planning artifacts
open real websocket or HTTP connections in tests
use float for money or quantities
silently drop unknown events or activities
run broad test suites or backtests
